title: What is 18 F-FDG PET/CT (Positron Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography)?
text: Positron Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography (PET / CT) is the latest examination technique, which combines two techniques to assess the anatomical structures and metabolic activity of different organs and tissues.

title: How to prepare for the examination?
text:
One day before the examination the following should be excluded:

  • Physical activity;
  • Foods high in carbohydrates (sugar, bakery, vegetables, fruits).

title: Examination day
text:
• Exclude food at least 4 hours before the examination, do not chew gum, and do not take soft drinks;
  • It is recommended to drink only large amounts of clean non-carbonated water.

title: How to come for the examination?
text:
• In comfortable shoes or sneakers;
  • In comfortable, warm clothing without metal parts;
  • With 1 liter of clean, non-carbonated drinking water;
  • With all medical records (results of previous imaging tests and/or DVDs, medical history);
  • With passport or identification card to complete the necessary documents.

title: How is the examination conducted?
text:
• It is necessary to be present at the examination at the appointed time;
  • It is necessary to keep silent in the PET center, turn off cell phones to ensure absolute rest of patients;
  • After a short conversation with the doctor, you will be provided with a comfortable sofa in a special room, where you should take a maximum relaxed position, close your eyes and relax;
  • Drink plenty of clean, non-carbonated water during rest;
  • At the doctor

title: How long does the whole examination process take (examination and preparation)?
text: Positron Emission Tomography of the whole body combined with Computed Tomography (PET/CT) takes from 4 to 4.5 hours (from the eyeball to the upper third of the thigh). It should be noted that after the examination, it is necessary to stay in the PET center for some time to bring the radiation dose to the allowable level.

title: What are the contraindications to the examination?
text:
• Pregnancy;
  • Breastfeeding mothers are advised not to breastfeed for at least 12 hours after the examination.
